title: I Took the Community-Choir Folder Checkout to the Section Lead Who Kept Four

parts.text: I arrived at 6:28 p.m. and alto folders 3 through 6 were tagged to section lead Priya with no return. The table card said: ONE FOLDER PER VOICE. RETURN AFTER REHEARSAL. I was forty-four, alto, holding empty hands. Priya palmed a fifth. "Leads are the score." I photographed the tags, the card, and the fifth. Then I logged a hoard. At 6:36 the director asked why Priya's name was on five folders. I let them finish the sentence they would regret in writing. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The director can see five alto folders tagged to Priya against the one-folder card.

social.video_title: The section lead kept four extra folders — Part 1/2
social.description: Community choir, empty hands, and a table card she posted. I logged the hoard. Would you have photographed the fifth?

parts.text: Priya called it marking until the director asked for the log. I printed the hoard, the photo, and the card. Four folders came back. Priya sang from one and told altos marking was always about optics. Optics is a word leads use when a fifth exists. Checkout now has a second line: LEADS ARE NOT THE LIBRARY. I keep folder 3. Priya returns. The table finally looks like music, not a stash. Nobody thanked me, which is how you know a policy finally works. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.

social.video_title: Leads are not the library — Part 2/2
social.description: Hoard log, returned folders, and a second line. Was marking ever five scores?
